## ✨ Highlights

HAProxy reloads without resetting the connections a proxy in front
keeps, and fresh upstreams.

- 🔁 **No reset at a reload behind a proxy**: `option idle-close-on-response`
  in a new node's defaults and in the examples - a balancer reusing its
  connections saw 262 and 281 of its requests fail over 45 reloads,
  none with it.
- ⏱️ **A reboot no longer waits for idle clients**: janusd ends HAProxy
  as soon as the requests it serves are answered.
- 📦 **Linux 7.3.5 and 6.18.64, AWS-LC 5.15.0, Docker Compose v5.8.0**.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Add `option idle-close-on-response` to your own configuration.** The
  configuration you apply replaces a new node's bootstrap: nodes already
  set up, and every configuration you keep, get it only by adding the
  line to each `defaults` section
  ([Reloads and idle connections](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md#reloads-and-idle-connections)).
  With it, the previous process of a reload lives until those
  connections send their next request or reach `timeout client`.

## 🔀 HAProxy

- **`option idle-close-on-response` in Janus's defaults**
  ([#675](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/675)): at a reload, the
  previous HAProxy process closed at once the connections it had
  accepted with no request in progress - idle keep-alive connections,
  and fresh ones whose first request was still on its way. A client
  whose request crossed that close met a reset: typically a proxy or a
  balancer in front, reusing its connections. Measured on 3.4 with
  45 reloads at 9,000 to 13,000 requests a second: 262 and 281 failed
  requests in front without the option, **none with it**. On the lab,
  reloading a node under keep-alive load: 10 and 20 failed requests
  through a keep-alive relay over 4 and 20 reloads without it, **0 of
  2.2 million** with it. It's in a new
  node's bootstrap configuration, the examples
  ([web.cfg](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/examples/haproxy/web.cfg))
  and the pages that show them.
- **A stop for good doesn't wait for idle clients**
  ([#675](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/675)): before a reboot,
  a shutdown or an update's reboot, janusd soft-stops HAProxy and waits
  for its clients to be served (up to 5 s). With the option, an idle
  keep-alive client would have held every reboot those 5 s: janusd now
  reads the requests in progress (`show sess`) just before the stop and
  waits only for those - a request in flight is still answered, with
  `Connection: close`. Measured: HAProxy stopped in **1.71 s instead of
  5.01 s** with an idle client and a request held 4 s, which got its
  200 - on the lab, **2.12 s instead of 7.02 s**, the API back 5 s
  sooner. Any doubt (the session list unreadable) waits as before.

## 📦 Components

- **Linux 7.3.5** (default track, was 7.3.4) and **6.18.64** (longterm,

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- `qemu-console-flood-test` measures again in three alternated rounds
  before failing on HAProxy's logging cost: a burst of load on the CI
  host during one measurement no longer fails it
  ([#673](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/673)).
- `qemu-cluster-upgrade-test` asks again a probe reset at a route
  change - what an update without the connection handoff does,
  documented - and still fails on anything else or on more resets than
  route changes ([#674](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/674)).
- `qemu-system-api-test` reboots with an idle keep-alive client and a
  request in flight ([#675](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/675)).
- v2026.11.17-2's lab campaign
  ([#667](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/667)) and notes
